chain.title: A machine for a planned area
chain.desc: Build and power the Builder, then choose a job before configuring its work area. Start with a small expendable test region and inspect the preview before allowing world changes.

chain.title: Describe the shape
chain.desc: Configure a Shape Card with the intended shape, dimensions, and offset. A valid card describes the work area; the Builder still needs power and appropriate materials or output storage.

chain.title: Build a small test structure
chain.desc: Insert the configured Shape Card, supply blocks and power, and use the supported preview to confirm placement. Run a small test build and confirm after the structure appears where intended.

chain.title: Choose a quarry card
chain.desc: Use a Quarry Shape Card to define a small mining region. Check its replacement behavior, power demand, filters, and output storage before expanding to a large area.

chain.title: An optional Fortune quarry
chain.desc: Upgrade to the Fortune quarry card when its harvest behavior suits the target blocks. Compare energy and output requirements before scaling the quarry.

chain.title: An optional Silk Touch quarry
chain.desc: Use the Silk Touch variant when you need blocks intact. This is an alternative to Fortune, so neither branch requires completing the other.

chain.title: Handle a fluid job
chain.desc: Configure the pump card and provide suitable fluid storage. Preview the region and test with a manageable volume before draining a large area.

chain.title: Record an existing shape
chain.desc: Configure the Scanner's region and scan a small structure first. Inspect the resulting shape data before using it in a larger construction workflow.

chain.title: Combine recorded shapes
chain.desc: Use the Composer to combine or modify available shape data. Keep a copy of the original scan so the result can be compared before construction.

chain.title: Preview the planned shape
chain.desc: Use the Projector with the supported shape data to inspect orientation and placement. A projected shape is a planning aid; it does not place building materials by itself.

chain.title: Mark a structure's bounds
chain.desc: Build the Space Chamber frame and controller in the documented arrangement. Define a small test structure before using a Builder operation that moves or copies blocks.

chain.title: Give the chamber its controller
chain.desc: Complete the Space Chamber and verify that its bounds are valid. The controller identifies the region for the card and Builder workflow.

chain.title: Link the selected chamber
chain.desc: Bind a Space Chamber Card to the correct chamber and configure the Builder job. Review destination and operation mode before running a move or copy.

chain.title: A separate shield project
chain.desc: Build a Shield Projector and prepare template blocks. This defensive and building utility branch does not require completing a quarry or moving a structure.

chain.title: Shape the shield boundary
chain.desc: Place connected shield template blocks in the desired shape, then configure the projector's filters and power supply. Test which entities may cross before using it in an occupied area.

chain.title: Expand the projector's capacity
chain.desc: Upgrade the projector when the planned shield needs more supported blocks or features. Check the new energy demand rather than treating a larger shield as free protection.

coverage.scope: Authored branched progression; item and component acquisition objectives, not automatic proof that a factory works.
limits: World operations require player preview and configuration; acquisition tasks cannot validate the selected area.
Mover and vehicle subsystems are not claimed as complete authored coverage.
Pack scripts, recipe changes, and other Minecraft versions require the installed-pack scan; this guide is not a complete mod manual.
coverage.verification: Local JAR item models and English registry names; selected recipes and bundled manuals checked. Not a new in-game playthrough.

notes: Re-reviewed 2026-10-07 against local Minecraft 1.20.1 JAR item assets and selected recipes/manuals, with official project sources listed separately. Every authored row now has explicit prerequisites; empty lists identify intentional branch roots. The coverage section states the verified versions and remaining limits. This replaces older list-order and item-count claims.
